position_in_era.geographic_locus: Almería (Tomatito) ↔ Santo Domingo / NYC (Camilo) — Barcelona Jazz Festival, 1998 (genesis)
position_in_era.historical_role: Lateral counterpart at the *piano-and-guitar* dialogue level: Tomatito (Camarón's longtime guitarist) and Dominican Latin-jazz pianist Michel Camilo improvising Chick Corea's 'Spain' and 'Bésame Mucho' at the Barcelona International Jazz Festival in 1998 — the same year Dorantes released *Orobroy*. The album *Spain* (2000) won the first Latin Grammy for Best Latin Jazz Album. Same translation logic, different pair, exact same era as the anchor.

narrative_slots.production_facts: Recorded after a 1998 Palau de la Música live performance. Released 2000 on Lola Records.
narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Tomatito had been Camarón's flamenco guitarist on *La leyenda del tiempo* (1979) and after; the Camilo collaboration is his post-Camarón translation work into jazz piano partnership.
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: Palau de la Música, Barcelona (1998 festival); subsequent international jazz-festival circuit.
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: Flamenco guitar (Tomatito) and piano (Camilo); duo and small-ensemble formats.
narrative_slots.release_circumstances: *Spain* (2000) won Best Latin Jazz Album at the inaugural Latin Grammys. Followed by *Spain Again* (2006) and *Spain Forever* (2016) — a sustained translation collaboration.
